comparisons.peer_summary: AMD provides CPUs, APUs, and chipsets for desktops and notebooks with AI capabilities and security features, and uses GPUs with software to power immersive gaming experiences.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and AMD describe their PC GPU businesses as serving gamers, creators, and immersive experiences. NVIDIA highlights the expanding market due to live streamers and generative AI for local usage, while AMD describes its discrete GPUs and APUs powering immersive gaming for PCs and consoles, including AI capabilities. Both explicitly link their hardware offerings to the PC gaming and creator demographic.

sentences.text: Gamers choose NVIDIA GPUs to enjoy immersive, increasingly cinematic virtual worlds.
In addition to serving the growing number of gamers, the market for PC GPUs is expanding because of the burgeoning population of live streamers, broadcasters, artists, and creators.

We drive innovation with our line-up of CPUs, APUs and chipsets for desktops and notebooks, to bring performance, efficiency, AI capabilities and modern security features to gamers, creators, consumers and enterprises.

Our GPUs, including discrete GPUs, semi-custom SoC products and development services, work together with software to power immersive gaming experiences for PCs, game consoles and cloud gaming services.

peer_results.rationale: None of Broadcom's candidates (Private AI solution, Competitive landscape) are substantively comparable to NVIDIA's specific disclosure regarding the Gaming and Creator Markets segment and the driver of local generative AI adoption on PCs. AVGO's candidate focuses on enterprise privacy/compliance solutions and general market competition, lacking the specific focus on the PC gaming/creator hardware market.

None of Intel's candidates (SEC Filing Cross-Reference, Foundry Business Strategy) are substantively comparable to NVIDIA's specific disclosure regarding the Gaming and Creator Markets. Intel's disclosed content relates to investor relations guidance and manufacturing strategy, not the end-user gaming/creator market dynamics.

comparisons.peer_topic: PC market and AI-driven DRAM demand
comparisons.peer_summary: Next-generation PCs feature AI capabilities and high-performance neural processing chipsets, leading to significantly higher DRAM content, with the company announcing low-power compression-attached memory modules to support AI workloads on PCs.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures identify the PC market as a key driver for next-generation hardware enabled by AI. NVIDIA notes that the PC GPU market is expanding because users are adopting generative AI applications locally on their PCs. Similarly, Micron states that next-generation PCs contain AI capabilities and high-performance neural processing chipsets, leading to significantly higher DRAM content to support these workloads. Both companies frame the AI-driven PC upgrade cycle as a primary growth vector for their respective components (GPUs for NVIDIA, DRAM for Micron).

sentences.text: With the advent of generative AI, we expect a broader set of PC users to choose NVIDIA GPUs for running generative AI applications locally on their PC, which is critical for privacy, latency, and cost-sensitive AI applications.
The next generation PCs that have been announced contain high-performance neural processing chipsets as well as AI.
We expect these devices will have significantly more DRAM content than today's average PC.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm envisions generative AI becoming ubiquitous, expanding beyond smartphones and PCs into industries such as IoT, XR, and automotive.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures discuss the expansion of AI capabilities into the PC market as a major business trend. NVIDIA expects a broader set of PC users to choose GPUs for running generative AI applications locally. Qualcomm envisions generative AI becoming ubiquitous, expanding from smartphones into PCs. Both companies identify the PC as a critical platform for the adoption of on-device generative AI.

sentences.text: With the advent of generative AI, we expect a broader set of PC users to choose NVIDIA GPUs for running generative AI applications locally on their PC, which is critical for privacy, latency, and cost-sensitive AI applications.
Building on the smartphone and PC foundation, we envision generative AI becoming ubiquitous, continuing to expand into industries and applications such as IoT, XR and automotive.
